- [Gleam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gleam_(programming_language))[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language)#cite_note-Gleam-23) | ## History ### 2006–2009: Early years [ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rust_(programming_language)&action=edit§ion=2)] According to _MIT Technology Review_, he started the project due to his frustration with a broken elevator in his apartment building whose software had crashed,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language)#cite_note-MITTechReview-24) and named the language after the [group of fungi of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(fungus)) that is "over-engineered for survival". [[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language)#cite_note-MITTechReview-24) During the time period between 2006 and 2009, Rust was not publicized to others at Mozilla and was written in Hoare's free time;[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language)#cite_note-Klabnik2016ACMHistory-25):7:50 Hoare began speaking about the language around 2009 after a small group at Mozilla became interested in the project. [[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language)#cite_note-Hoare2010-26) He described the language as "technology from the past come to save the future from itself." [[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language)#cite_note-Klabnik2016ACMHistory-25):8:17[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language)#cite_note-Hoare2010-26) Early Rust developer Manish Goregaokar similarly described Rust as being based on "mostly decades-old research." [[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language)#cite_note-Klabnik2016ACMHistory-25):15:34[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language)#cite_note-OCamlCompiler-27) Early Rust contained several features no longer present today, including explicit [object-oriented programming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Object-oriented_programming) via an `obj` keyword[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language)#cite_note-Klabnik2016ACMHistory-25):10:08 and a [typestates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Typestate_analysis) system for variable state changes, such as going from uninitialized to initialized. ## Adoption [ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rust_(programming_language)&action=edit§ion=44)] In [web services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_service), [OpenDNS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OpenDNS), a [DNS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNS) resolution service owned by [Cisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cisco), uses Rust internally.[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language)#cite_note-168)[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language)#cite_note-169) [Amazon Web Services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_Web_Services) uses Rust in "performance-sensitive components" of services. [[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language)#cite_note-171) Microsoft also uses Rust to run containerized modules with [WebAssembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WebAssembly) and [Kubernetes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kubernetes).[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language)#cite_note-172) [Cloudflare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloudflare), a company providing [content delivery network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Content_delivery_network) services, used Rust to build a new [web proxy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_proxy) named Pingora for increased performance and efficiency. [[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language)#cite_note-174)[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language)#cite_note-175)[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language)#cite_note-176) [[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language)#cite_note-UsenixRustForLinux-177)[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language)#cite_note-178)[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language)#cite_note-179) The first drivers written in Rust were included in version 6.8. [[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language)#cite_note-180) The [Android](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Android_(operating_system)) developers used Rust in 2021 to rewrite existing components.[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language)#cite_note-181)[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language)#cite_note-182) [Microsoft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft) has rewritten parts of [Windows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windows) in Rust. [[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language)#cite_note-183) The r9 project aims to re-implement [Plan 9 from Bell Labs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plan_9_from_Bell_Labs) in Rust. [[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language)#cite_note-184) Rust has also been used in the development of new operating systems such as [Redox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Redox_(operating_system)), a "Unix-like" operating system and [microkernel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microkernel),[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language)#cite_note-185) Theseus, an experimental operating system with modular state management,[[180]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language)#cite_note-186)[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language)#cite_note-187) and most of [Fuchsia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fuchsia_(operating_system)). [[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language)#cite_note-rustmag-1-188) Rust is used for command-line tools and operating system components such as [stratisd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stratis_(configuration_daemon)), a [file system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File_system) manager[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language)#cite_note-189)[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language)#cite_note-190) and COSMIC, a [desktop environment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desktop_environment) by [System76](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/System76). [[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language)#cite_note-191) [[186]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language)#cite_note-192) Other notable adoptions in this space include [Ruffle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruffle_(software)), an open-source [SWF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SWF) emulator,[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language)#cite_note-193) and [Polkadot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polkadot_(cryptocurrency)), an open source [blockchain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blockchain) and [cryptocurrency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cryptocurrency) platform. [[190]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language)#cite_note-196)[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language)#cite_note-197) [[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language)#cite_note-MITTechReview-24) [[192]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language)#cite_note-SO-2025-survey-198) ## Community ### Rust Foundation [ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rust_(programming_language)&action=edit§ion=47)] | Type | [501(c)(6)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/501(c)(6)) organization[[201]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language)#cite_note-208) | [[202]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language)#cite_note-209)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language)#cite_note-:4-51) [[206]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language)#cite_note-213) ## See also - [Outline of the Rust programming language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outline_of_the_Rust_programming_language) ## References ### Others 3. # Rust Tutorial
## Learn Rust
Rust is a popular programming language used to build everything from web servers to game engines.

Rust is known for being very fast, and is similar to [C](https://www.w3schools.com/c/index.php) and [C++](https://www.w3schools.com/cpp/default.asp) in language.
